    42→import { handleError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandler';
    43→import { useGalleryFilterState } from '@/shared/hooks/gallery/useGalleryFilterState';
    44→
    45→interface UseGenerationsPageLogicOptions {
    46→  itemsPerPage?: number;
    47→  mediaType?: 'all' | 'image' | 'video';
    48→  toolType?: string;
    49→  enableDataLoading?: boolean;
    50→}
    51→
    52→/**
    53→ * @internal Use `useGalleryPageState` instead (exported alias below).
    54→ */
    55→function useGenerationsPageLogic({
    56→  itemsPerPage = 45,
    57→  mediaType = 'image',
    58→  toolType,
    59→  enableDataLoading = true
    60→}: UseGenerationsPageLogicOptions = {}) {
    61→  const { selectedProjectId } = useProject();
    62→  const { shots: shotsData } = useShots();
    63→
    64→  // Gate all data loading based on project availability and enableDataLoading flag
    65→  const shouldLoadData = enableDataLoading && !!selectedProjectId;
    66→  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
    67→
    68→  const { currentShotId } = useCurrentShot();
    69→
    70→  // Get last affected shot context early so it's available for effects below
    71→  const lastAffectedShotContext = useContext(LastAffectedShotContext);
    72→  const { lastAffectedShotId = null, setLastAffectedShotId = () => {} } = lastAffectedShotContext || {};
    73→
    74→  // ============================================================================
    75→  // FILTER STATE (extracted to useGalleryFilterState)
    76→  // ============================================================================
    77→
    78→  const filterState = useGalleryFilterState({
    79→    shouldLoadData,
    80→    onShotFilterApplied: setLastAffectedShotId,
    81→  }, mediaType, toolType);
    82→
    83→  const {
    84→    selectedShotFilter,
    85→    excludePositioned,
    86→    searchTerm,
    87→    starredOnly,
    88→    filters,
    89→    expectedItemCount,
    90→    applyQueryFallback,
    91→  } = filterState;
    92→
    93→  // Reset to page 1 when shot filter or position filter changes
    94→  useEffect(() => {
    95→    setPage(1);
    96→  }, [selectedShotFilter, excludePositioned]);
    97→
    98→  // Reset to page 1 when media type or starred filter changes
    99→  useEffect(() => {
   100→    setPage(1);
   101→  }, [mediaType, starredOnly]);
   102→
   103→  // ============================================================================
   104→  // DATA FETCHING
   105→  // ============================================================================
   106→
   107→  const generationsQuery = useProjectGenerations(
   108→    shouldLoadData ? selectedProjectId : null,
   109→    page,
   110→    itemsPerPage,
   111→    shouldLoadData,
   112→    filters
   113→  );
   114→  const generationsResponse = generationsQuery.data as GenerationsPaginatedResponse | undefined;
   115→  const isFetching = generationsQuery.isFetching;
   116→  const isError = generationsQuery.isError;
   117→  const error = generationsQuery.error;
   118→
   119→  // Track if we're showing stale/placeholder data during a filter change
   120→  const isPlaceholderData = generationsQuery.isPlaceholderData;
   121→
   122→  // Show loading state when:
   123→  // 1. Initial load (no data yet), OR
   124→  // 2. Filter changed and we're showing stale placeholder data
   125→  const isLoading = generationsQuery.isLoading || (isFetching && isPlaceholderData);
   126→
   127→
   128→  // ============================================================================
   129→  // QUERY FALLBACK - delegate to filter state hook
   130→  // ============================================================================
   131→
   132→  useEffect(() => {
   133→    applyQueryFallback({
   134→      isLoading,
   135→      isFetching,
   136→      total: generationsResponse?.total,
   137→      hasResponse: generationsResponse !== undefined,
   138→    }, page);
   139→  }, [selectedShotFilter, isLoading, isFetching, generationsResponse?.total, page, applyQueryFallback, generationsResponse]);
   140→
   141→  // ============================================================================
   142→  // MUTATIONS
   143→  // ============================================================================
   144→
   145→  const addImageToShotMutation = useAddImageToShot();
   146→  const addImageToShotWithoutPositionMutation = useAddImageToShotWithoutPosition();
   147→  const positionExistingGenerationMutation = usePositionExistingGenerationInShot();
   148→  const deleteGenerationMutation = useDeleteGeneration();
   149→  const toggleStarMutation = useToggleGenerationStar();
   150→
   151→  // ============================================================================
   152→  // PAGINATION
   153→  // ============================================================================
   154→
   155→  const paginatedData = useMemo(() => {
   156→    const items = generationsResponse?.items ?? [];
   157→    const total = generationsResponse?.total ?? 0;
   158→    const totalPages = Math.ceil(total / itemsPerPage);
   159→
   160→    return {
   161→      items,
   162→      totalPages,
   163→      currentPage: page
   164→    };
   165→  }, [generationsResponse, page, itemsPerPage]);
   166→
   167→  // ============================================================================
   168→  // LAST AFFECTED SHOT INITIALIZATION
   169→  // ============================================================================
   170→
   171→  useEffect(() => {
   172→
   173→    if (!lastAffectedShotId && shotsData && shotsData.length > 0) {
   174→      setLastAffectedShotId(shotsData[0].id);
   175→    }
   176→  }, [lastAffectedShotId, shotsData, setLastAffectedShotId, currentShotId, selectedShotFilter]);
   177→
   178→  // ============================================================================
   179→  // ACTION HANDLERS
   180→  // ============================================================================
   181→
   182→  const handleServerPageChange = (newPage: number) => {
   183→    setPage(newPage);
   184→  };
   185→
   186→  const handleDeleteGeneration = (id: string) => {
   187→    deleteGenerationMutation.mutate(id);
   188→  };
   189→
   190→  const handleToggleStar = (id: string, starred: boolean) => {
   191→    toggleStarMutation.mutate({ id, starred });
   192→  };
   193→
   194→  const handleAddToShot = async (generationId: string, imageUrl?: string, thumbUrl?: string): Promise<boolean> => {
   195→    const targetShotId = lastAffectedShotId || currentShotId;
   196→
   197→    if (!targetShotId || !selectedProjectId) {
   198→      toast.error("No shot selected", {
   199→        description: "Please select a shot in the gallery or create one first.",
   200→      });
   201→      return false;
   202→    }
   203→
   204→    const shouldPositionExisting = selectedShotFilter === targetShotId && excludePositioned;
   205→
   206→    // Dispatch event to trigger skeleton animation in ShotListDisplay
   207→    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('shot-pending-upload', {
   208→      detail: { shotId: targetShotId, expectedCount: 1 }
   209→    }));
   210→
   211→    try {
   212→      if (shouldPositionExisting) {
   213→
   214→        await positionExistingGenerationMutation.mutateAsync({
   215→          shot_id: targetShotId,
   216→          generation_id: generationId,
   217→          project_id: selectedProjectId,
   218→        });
   219→
   220→      } else {
   221→
   222→        await addImageToShotMutation.mutateAsync({
   223→          shot_id: targetShotId,
   224→          generation_id: generationId,
   225→          imageUrl: imageUrl,
   226→          thumbUrl: thumbUrl,
   227→          project_id: selectedProjectId,
   228→        });
   229→
   230→      }
   231→
   232→      return true;
   233→    } catch (error) {
   234→      handleError(error, { context: 'useGenerationsPageLogic', toastTitle: 'Failed to add image to shot' });
   235→      return false;
   236→    }
   237→  };
   238→
   239→  const handleAddToShotWithoutPosition = async (generationId: string, imageUrl?: string, thumbUrl?: string): Promise<boolean> => {
   240→    const targetShotId = lastAffectedShotId || currentShotId;
   241→
   242→    if (!targetShotId || !selectedProjectId) {
   243→      toast.error("No shot selected", {
   244→        description: "Please select a shot in the gallery or create one first.",
   245→      });
   246→      return false;
   247→    }
   248→
   249→    try {
   250→      await addImageToShotWithoutPositionMutation.mutateAsync({
   251→        shot_id: targetShotId,
   252→        generation_id: generationId,
   253→        imageUrl: imageUrl,
   254→        thumbUrl: thumbUrl,
   255→        project_id: selectedProjectId,
   256→      });
   257→      return true;
   258→    } catch (error) {
   259→      handleError(error, { context: 'useGenerationsPageLogic', toastTitle: 'Failed to add image to shot' });
   260→      return false;
   261→    }
   262→  };
   263→
   264→  // ============================================================================
   265→  // RETURN API
   266→  // ============================================================================
   267→
   268→  return {
   269→    // Data
   270→    selectedProjectId,
   271→    shotsData,
   272→    generationsResponse,
   273→    paginatedData,
   274→    lastAffectedShotId,
   275→    totalCount: generationsResponse?.total ?? 0,
   276→
   277→    // State
   278→    page,
   279→    selectedShotFilter,
   280→    excludePositioned,
   281→    searchTerm,
   282→    starredOnly,
   283→
   284→    // State setters
   285→    setPage,
   286→    setSelectedShotFilter: filterState.setSelectedShotFilter,
   287→    setExcludePositioned: filterState.setExcludePositioned,
   288→    setSearchTerm: filterState.setSearchTerm,
   289→    setStarredOnly: filterState.setStarredOnly,
   290→
   291→    // Loading states
   292→    isLoading,
   293→    isFetching,
   294→    isError,
   295→    error,
   296→    isDeleting: deleteGenerationMutation.isPending ? deleteGenerationMutation.variables as string : null,
   297→
   298→    // For skeleton display when filter changes

   301→    // Handlers

  "content": "import React from 'react';\nimport { Button } from '@/shared/components/ui/button';\nimport { AlertTriangle, RefreshCw, Home } from 'lucide-react';\n\ninterface ToolErrorBoundaryState {\n  hasError: boolean;\n  error: Error | null;\n  errorInfo: React.ErrorInfo | null;\n}\n\ninterface ToolErrorBoundaryProps {\n  toolName: string;\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n}\n\n/**\n * Per-tool error boundary that catches errors within a single tool's route\n * and displays a recovery UI instead of crashing the entire app.\n *\n * Wrap each tool's page element in routes.tsx so that one tool's crash\n * doesn't take down unrelated UI (header, panes, other tools).\n */\nexport class ToolErrorBoundary extends React.Component<\n  ToolErrorBoundaryProps,\n  ToolErrorBoundaryState\n> {\n  constructor(props: ToolErrorBoundaryProps) {\n    super(props);\n    this.state = {\n      hasError: false,\n      error: null,\n      errorInfo: null,\n    };\n  }\n\n  static getDerivedStateFromError(error: Error): Partial<ToolErrorBoundaryState> {\n    return { hasError: true, error };\n  }\n\n  componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: React.ErrorInfo): void {\n    console.error(`[ToolErrorBoundary:${this.props.toolName}] Uncaught error:`, {\n      message: error.message,\n      name: error.name,\n      stack: error.stack?.split('\\n').slice(0, 5).join('\\n'),\n      componentStack: errorInfo.componentStack?.split('\\n').slice(0, 10).join('\\n'),\n    });\n\n    this.setState({ errorInfo });\n  }\n\n  handleRetry = (): void => {\n    this.setState({\n      hasError: false,\n      error: null,\n      errorInfo: null,\n    });\n  };\n\n  render(): React.ReactNode {\n    if (this.state.hasError) {\n      const { error } = this.state;\n      const { toolName } = this.props;\n      const isDev = import.meta.env.DEV;\n\n      return (\n        <div className=\"flex items-center justify-center p-8 min-h-[50vh]\">\n          <div className=\"max-w-md w-full space-y-6 text-center\">\n            <div className=\"flex justify-center\">\n              <div className=\"rounded-full bg-destructive/10 p-3\">\n                <AlertTriangle className=\"h-8 w-8 text-destructive\" />\n              </div>\n            </div>\n\n            <div className=\"space-y-2\">\n              <h2 className=\"text-xl font-semibold text-foreground\">\n                {toolName} encountered an error\n              </h2>\n              <p className=\"text-sm text-muted-foreground\">\n                Something went wrong in this tool. Your other tools and data are unaffected.\n              </p>\n            </div>\n\n            {isDev && error && (\n              <div className=\"bg-muted rounded-lg p-4 text-left\">\n                <p className=\"text-sm font-mono text-destructive break-all\">\n                  {error.name}: {error.message}\n                </p>\n                {error.stack && (\n                  <pre className=\"mt-2 text-xs text-muted-foreground overflow-x-auto max-h-32\">\n                    {error.stack.split('\\n').slice(1, 6).join('\\n')}\n                  </pre>\n                )}\n              </div>\n            )}\n\n            <div className=\"flex flex-col sm:flex-row gap-3 justify-center\">\n              <Button onClick={this.handleRetry} variant=\"default\">\n                <RefreshCw className=\"h-4 w-4 mr-2\" />\n                Try Again\n              </Button>\n              <Button variant=\"outline\" asChild>\n                <a href=\"/\">\n                  <Home className=\"h-4 w-4 mr-2\" />\n                  Go Home\n                </a>\n              </Button>\n            </div>\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      );\n    }\n\n    return this.props.children;\n  }\n}\n"
}

This action cannot be undone.\"\n      confirmText=\"Delete\"\n      destructive\n      onConfirm={handleConfirm}\n    />\n  );\n\n  return {\n    /** Opens the confirmation dialog for the given generation ID */\n    requestDelete,\n    /** Render this element in your component tree to show the dialog */\n    confirmDialog,\n    /** Whether a delete is currently in progress */\n    isPending: deleteGenerationMutation.isPending,\n    /** The ID currently being deleted (or null) */\n    deletingId: deleteGenerationMutation.isPending ? (deleteGenerationMutation.variables as string) : null,\n  };\n}\n"
}

I see the pattern. The `onDelete` prop flows through `MediaGallery` and eventually reaches individual items. The cleanest approach given that this is a hook, not a component, is to change the approach slightly.

Instead of a hook that returns JSX, I'll modify `useGalleryPageState` and the other call sites to use a pattern where:
1. The hook returns `requestDeleteGeneration` (opens dialog) + `deleteConfirmState` (state for rendering dialog)
2. The consuming component renders the `ConfirmDialog`

But actually, the simplest and most consistent approach is to make `useDeleteGenerationWithConfirm` return the state values instead of JSX, so any hook can use it, and the component that renders can create the dialog from the state.

(deleteGenerationMutation.variables as string) : null,\n  };\n}\n"

## Fix #14 -- Pagination empty range guard

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaGallery/hooks/useMediaGalleryPagination.ts` (line 161)

When `totalFilteredItems === 0`, `rangeStart` is correctly set to 0, but `rangeEnd` was computed as `0 + 0 - 1 = -1`. Added a guard so `rangeEnd` is clamped to 0 when there are no items:

```ts
const rangeEnd = totalFilteredItems === 0 ? 0 : rangeStart + displayedCount - 1;
```

## Fix #12 -- clearNavigation dependency array

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaGallery/hooks/useMediaGalleryPagination.ts` (line 193)

The `clearNavigation` callback body only calls `setNavigationState` and `clearTimeout` -- it never reads `navigationState.status` or `navigationState.direction`. Changed the dependency array from `[navigationState.status, navigationState.direction]` to `[]` to prevent unnecessary re-creation.

## Fix #23 -- deepEqual try-catch

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/deepEqual.ts` (lines 26-32)

Wrapped the `JSON.stringify` comparison in a try-catch block. On error (e.g., circular references), the function now returns `false` instead of throwing.

    28→async function uploadVideoWithPoster(file: File): Promise<{ videoUrl: string; posterUrl: string }> {
    29→  const posterBlob = await extractVideoPosterFrame(file);
    30→
    31→  const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
    32→  if (!session?.user?.id) {
    33→    throw new Error('User not authenticated');
    34→  }
    35→  const userId = session.user.id;
    36→
    37→  const fileExt = getFileExtension(file.name, file.type, 'mp4');
    38→  const timestamp = Date.now();
    39→  const randomId = Math.random().toString(36).substring(7);
    40→  const fileName = storagePaths.upload(userId, `${timestamp}-${randomId}.${fileExt}`);
    41→  const posterFileName = storagePaths.thumbnail(userId, `${timestamp}-${randomId}-poster.jpg`);
    42→
    43→  const { error: videoError } = await supabase.storage
    44→    .from(MEDIA_BUCKET)
    45→    .upload(fileName, file, { cacheControl: '3600', upsert: false });
    46→  if (videoError) throw videoError;
    47→
    48→  const { error: posterError } = await supabase.storage
    49→    .from(MEDIA_BUCKET)
    50→    .upload(posterFileName, posterBlob, {
    51→      cacheControl: '3600',
    52→      upsert: false,
    53→      contentType: 'image/jpeg'
    54→    });
    55→  if (posterError) throw posterError;
    56→
    57→  const { data: { publicUrl: videoUrl } } = supabase.storage
    58→    .from(MEDIA_BUCKET)
    59→    .getPublicUrl(fileName);
    60→  const { data: { publicUrl: posterUrl } } = supabase.storage
    61→    .from(MEDIA_BUCKET)
    62→    .getPublicUrl(posterFileName);
    63→
    64→  return { videoUrl, posterUrl };
    65→}

   260→      setCharacterImageLoaded(false);

   267→
   268→  // Shared video upload logic (file picker + drag-drop)
   269→  const processVideoUpload = async (file: File) => {
   270→    await videoUpload.execute(async () => {

   273→      setMotionVideoPlaying(false);

   279→  };
   280→
   281→  // Handle character image upload (file picker)
   282→  const handleCharacterImageUpload = async (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
   283→    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
   284→    if (!file) return;
   285→    if (!['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/jpg'].includes(file.type)) {

   294→    const file = e.target.files?.[0];

   302→

   315→  // Drag and drop handlers for character image

   329→    );

   332→    }

   334→

   339→    const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect();
   340→    const x = e.clientX;
   341→    const y = e.clientY;
   342→    if (x < rect.left || x >= rect.right || y < rect.top || y >= rect.bottom) {
   343→      setIsDraggingOverImage(false);
   344→    }
   345→  };
   346→
   347→  const handleImageDrop = async (e: React.DragEvent) => {

   361→  // Drag and drop handlers for motion video

   537→              >

   752→                  config={{

   770→          // While loading for the first time, don't show anything
   771→          return null;
   772→        })()}
   773→      </div>
   774→    </PageFadeIn>
   775→  );
   776→};
   777→
   778→export default CharacterAnimatePage;

1→import { useState, useCallback } from 'react';
     2→import { useDeleteGeneration } from '@/shared/hooks/useGenerationMutations';
     3→import { ConfirmDialog } from '@/shared/components/ConfirmDialog';
     4→
     5→/**
     6→ * Wraps useDeleteGeneration with a confirmation dialog.
     7→ *
     8→ * Returns `requestDelete(id)` which opens the dialog, and a
     9→ * `DeleteConfirmDialog` component that must be rendered by the caller.
    10→ *
    11→ * Works in both hooks and components:
    12→ * - Hooks: return `requestDelete` and `DeleteConfirmDialog` to the consuming component
    13→ * - Components: call `requestDelete` and render `<DeleteConfirmDialog />` directly
    14→ *
    15→ * @example
    16→ * ```tsx
    17→ * const { requestDelete, DeleteConfirmDialog, isPending } = useDeleteGenerationWithConfirm();
    18→ *
    19→ * return (
    20→ *   <>
    21→ *     <button onClick={() => requestDelete(id)}>Delete</button>
    22→ *     <DeleteConfirmDialog />
    23→ *   </>
    24→ * );
    25→ * ```
    26→ */
    27→export function useDeleteGenerationWithConfirm() {
    28→  const deleteGenerationMutation = useDeleteGeneration();
    29→  const [pendingDeleteId, setPendingDeleteId] = useState<string | null>(null);
    30→
    31→  const requestDelete = useCallback((id: string) => {
    32→    setPendingDeleteId(id);
    33→  }, []);
    34→
    35→  const handleConfirm = useCallback(() => {
    36→    if (pendingDeleteId) {
    37→      deleteGenerationMutation.mutate(pendingDeleteId);
    38→      setPendingDeleteId(null);
    39→    }
    40→  }, [pendingDeleteId, deleteGenerationMutation]);
    41→
    42→  const handleOpenChange = useCallback((open: boolean) => {
    43→    if (!open) {
    44→      setPendingDeleteId(null);
    45→    }
    46→  }, []);
    47→
    48→  /** Render this in your component tree to show the confirmation dialog */
    49→  const DeleteConfirmDialog = useCallback(() => (
    50→    <ConfirmDialog
    51→      open={pendingDeleteId !== null}
    52→      onOpenChange={handleOpenChange}
    53→      title="Delete Generation"
    54→      description="Are you sure you want to delete this generation? This action cannot be undone."
    55→      confirmText="Delete"
    56→      destructive
    57→      onConfirm={handleConfirm}
    58→    />
    59→  ), [pendingDeleteId, handleOpenChange, handleConfirm]);
    60→
    61→  return {
    62→    /** Opens the confirmation dialog for the given generation ID */
    63→    requestDelete,
    64→    /** Render this component in your JSX tree: `<DeleteConfirmDialog />` */
    65→    DeleteConfirmDialog,
    66→    /** Whether a delete is currently in progress */
    67→    isPending: deleteGenerationMutation.isPending,
    68→    /** The ID currently being deleted (or null) */
    69→    deletingId: deleteGenerationMutation.isPending ? (deleteGenerationMutation.variables as string) : null,
    70→  };
    71→}

## Summary of all three fixes

### Fix #7 -- visibilitychange flush for settings write queue

**File modified:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/settingsWriteQueue.ts` (lines 193-206)

**Change:** Added a `visibilitychange` event listener alongside the existing `beforeunload` listener. When `document.visibilityState` becomes `'hidden'` (tab switch, app backgrounding on mobile), `flushAll()` is called to write any pending settings. This addresses the fact that mobile browsers (especially iOS Safari) do not reliably fire `beforeunload` when switching tabs or backgrounding the app.

The existing `beforeunload` listener is preserved as a fallback for desktop close scenarios. Both listeners share the same `typeof window !== 'undefined'` SSR guard.

---

### Fix #20 -- Per-tool error boundaries

**Files created:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/ToolErrorBoundary.tsx` -- New class-based React error boundary component

**Files modified:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/app/routes.tsx` -- Wrapped all 7 tool routes with `<ToolErrorBoundary>`

**Design decisions:**
- Modeled after the existing `AppErrorBoundary` (same design tokens, similar structure, class-based with `getDerivedStateFromError` and `componentDidCatch`)
- Takes a `toolName` prop to display which tool crashed in the error message
- Shows "Try Again" (resets error state) and "Go Home" (navigates to `/`) buttons
- Dev-only error details (stack trace) matching the `AppErrorBoundary` pattern
- Uses project design tokens: `bg-destructive/10`, `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`, `bg-muted`, etc.
- Renders in the content area (`min-h-[50vh]`) rather than full screen, so the app chrome (header, panes) remains functional
- Error logging includes the tool name: `[ToolErrorBoundary:Video Travel]`

All 7 tool routes are wrapped: Image Generation, Video Travel, Character Animate, Join Clips, Edit Images, Edit Video, Training Data Helper. The `ToolErrorBoundary` wraps outside `Suspense` for lazy-loaded tools so chunk load errors also get caught by the tool boundary before reaching the app-level one.

---

   131→export async function createSingleItemVariant(
   132→  ctx: HandlerContext,
   133→  parentGenerationId: string
   134→): Promise<any | null> {
   135→  const { supabase, taskId, taskData, publicUrl, thumbnailUrl, childOrder } = ctx;
   136→
   137→  // Check if this is first variant on parent
   138→  const { count: existingVariantCount } = await supabase
   139→    .from('generation_variants')
   140→    .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
   141→    .eq('generation_id', parentGenerationId);
   142→  const isFirstVariant = (existingVariantCount || 0) === 0;
   143→
   144→  const toolType = taskData.params?.full_orchestrator_payload?.tool_type ||
   145→                   taskData.params?.tool_type ||
   146→                   taskData.tool_type;
   147→
   148→  const variantType = taskData.variant_type || 'edit';
   149→
   150→  const result = await createVariantOnParent(
   151→    supabase, parentGenerationId, publicUrl, thumbnailUrl, taskData, taskId,
   152→    variantType,
   153→    {
   154→      tool_type: toolType,
   155→      created_from: 'single_item_completion',
   156→      is_single_item: true,
   157→      child_order: childOrder ?? 0,
   158→    },
   159→    null,
   160→    isFirstVariant
   161→  );
   162→
   163→  return result;
   164→}

   166→/**
   167→ * Find existing generation at a position (for variant creation)
   168→ */
   169→export async function findExistingGenerationAtPosition(
   170→  supabase: any,
   171→  parentGenerationId: string,
   172→  childOrder: number,
   173→  pairShotGenId?: string
   174→): Promise<string | null> {
   175→  console.log(`[GenHandler] Checking for existing generation at segment_index=${childOrder}, pair_shot_gen_id=${pairShotGenId || 'none'}`);
   176→
   177→  // Strategy 1: Try to find by pair_shot_generation_id column
   178→  if (pairShotGenId) {
   179→    // Match by the FK column (source of truth with referential integrity)
   180→    const { data: matchByColumn, error: matchByColumnError } = await supabase
   181→      .from('generations')
   182→      .select('id')
   183→      .eq('parent_generation_id', parentGenerationId)
   184→      .eq('is_child', true)
   185→      .eq('pair_shot_generation_id', pairShotGenId)
   186→      .maybeSingle();
   187→
   188→    if (!matchByColumnError && matchByColumn?.id) {
   189→      console.log(`[GenHandler] Found match by pair_shot_generation_id column: ${matchByColumn.id}`);
   190→      return matchByColumn.id;
   191→    }
   192→
   193→    // NOTE: We intentionally DON'T fall back to params JSONB here.
   194→    // Pre-migration generations have already been migrated to the column.
   195→    // Any generation with NULL column but non-NULL params is orphaned
   196→    // (FK cascade set column to NULL when shot_generation was deleted).
   197→    console.log(`[GenHandler] No match by pair_shot_generation_id column`);
   198→  }
   199→
   200→  // Strategy 2: Fallback to child_order match
   201→  // IMPORTANT: Only use this fallback when NO pair_shot_generation_id was provided
   202→  // If pairShotGenId was provided but no match found, DON'T fall back to child_order
   203→  // because the existing child at that index may be for a different timeline layout
   204→  if (!pairShotGenId) {
   205→    const { data: matchByChildOrder, error: matchByChildOrderError } = await supabase
   206→      .from('generations')
   207→      .select('id')
   208→      .eq('parent_generation_id', parentGenerationId)
   209→      .eq('is_child', true)
   210→      .eq('child_order', childOrder)
   211→      .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
   212→      .limit(1)
   213→      .maybeSingle();
   214→
   215→    if (!matchByChildOrderError && matchByChildOrder?.id) {
   216→      console.log(`[GenHandler] Found match by child_order=${childOrder}: ${matchByChildOrder.id}`);
   217→      return matchByChildOrder.id;
   218→    }
   219→  } else {
   220→    console.log(`[GenHandler] No match by pair_shot_generation_id, skipping child_order fallback (would match wrong slot after timeline rearrangement)`);
   221→  }
   222→
   223→  console.log(`[GenHandler] No existing generation found at position`);
   224→  return null;
   225→}

   548→/**
   549→ * Extract segment-specific params from expanded arrays in orchestrator_details.
   550→ * For travel segments, each segment can have different prompts, frame counts, etc.
   551→ */
   552→export function extractSegmentSpecificParams(
   553→  params: any,
   554→  orchDetails: any,
   555→  segmentIndex: number
   556→): any {
   557→  const specificParams = { ...params };
   558→
   559→  const specificPrompt = extractFromArray(orchDetails.base_prompts_expanded, segmentIndex);
   560→  if (specificPrompt !== undefined) {
   561→    specificParams.prompt = specificPrompt;
   562→    console.log(`[GenMigration] Set child prompt: "${String(specificPrompt).substring(0, 20)}..."`);
   563→  }
   564→
   565→  const specificNegativePrompt = extractFromArray(orchDetails.negative_prompts_expanded, segmentIndex);
   566→  if (specificNegativePrompt !== undefined) {
   567→    specificParams.negative_prompt = specificNegativePrompt;
   568→  }
   569→
   570→  const specificFrames = extractFromArray(orchDetails.segment_frames_expanded, segmentIndex);
   571→  if (specificFrames !== undefined) {
   572→    specificParams.num_frames = specificFrames;
   573→  }
   574→
   575→  const specificOverlap = extractFromArray(orchDetails.frame_overlap_expanded, segmentIndex);
   576→  if (specificOverlap !== undefined) {
   577→    specificParams.frame_overlap = specificOverlap;
   578→  }
   579→
   580→  const pairShotGenId = extractFromArray(orchDetails.pair_shot_generation_ids, segmentIndex);
   581→  if (pairShotGenId !== undefined) {
   582→    specificParams.pair_shot_generation_id = pairShotGenId;
   583→    console.log(`[GenMigration] Set pair_shot_generation_id: ${pairShotGenId}`);
   584→  }
   585→
   586→  const startImageGenId = extractFromArray(orchDetails.input_image_generation_ids, segmentIndex);
   587→  if (startImageGenId !== undefined) {
   588→    specificParams.start_image_generation_id = startImageGenId;
   589→  }
   590→  const endImageGenId = extractFromArray(orchDetails.input_image_generation_ids, segmentIndex + 1);
   591→  if (endImageGenId !== undefined) {
   592→    specificParams.end_image_generation_id = endImageGenId;
   593→  }
   594→
   595→  return specificParams;
   596→}

    23→// Pricing constants for video_enhance task (fal.ai rates)
    24→const VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING = {
    25→  // FILM (interpolation): $0.0013 per compute second
    26→  FILM_COST_PER_SECOND: 0.0013,
    27→  // FlashVSR (upscale): $0.0005 per megapixel (width × height × frames / 1,000,000)
    28→  FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL: 0.0005,
    29→};
    30→
    31→// Special cost calculation for video_enhance task
    32→// Combines FILM (time-based) and FlashVSR (megapixel-based) pricing
    33→function calculateVideoEnhanceCost(taskParams: any): { cost: number; breakdown: any } {
    34→  let totalCost = 0;
    35→  const breakdown: any = {};
    36→
    37→  // Get result data from task params (worker should populate this)
    38→  const result = taskParams?.result || taskParams;
    39→
    40→  // FILM interpolation cost: $0.0013 per compute second
    41→  if (result?.interpolation_compute_seconds && result.interpolation_compute_seconds > 0) {
    42→    const filmCost = VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FILM_COST_PER_SECOND * result.interpolation_compute_seconds;
    43→    totalCost += filmCost;
    44→    breakdown.interpolation = {
    45→      compute_seconds: result.interpolation_compute_seconds,
    46→      cost_per_second: VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FILM_COST_PER_SECOND,
    47→      cost: Math.round(filmCost * 1000000) / 1000000,
    48→    };
    49→  }
    50→
    51→  // FlashVSR upscale cost: $0.0005 per megapixel
    52→  if (result?.output_width && result?.output_height && result?.output_frames) {
    53→    const megapixels = (result.output_width * result.output_height * result.output_frames) / 1_000_000;
    54→    const upscaleCost = VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL * megapixels;
    55→    totalCost += upscaleCost;
    56→    breakdown.upscale = {
    57→      output_width: result.output_width,
    58→      output_height: result.output_height,
    59→      output_frames: result.output_frames,
    60→      megapixels: Math.round(megapixels * 100) / 100,
    61→      cost_per_megapixel: VIDEO_ENHANCE_PRICING.FLASHVSR_COST_PER_MEGAPIXEL,
    62→      cost: Math.round(upscaleCost * 1000000) / 1000000,
    63→    };
    64→  }
    65→
    66→  return {
    67→    cost: Math.round(totalCost * 1000000) / 1000000,
    68→    breakdown,
    69→  };
    70→}
    71→
    72→// Calculate cost based on billing type and task configuration
    73→function calculateTaskCost(
    74→  taskType: string,
    75→  billingType: string,
    76→  baseCostPerSecond: number,
    77→  unitCost: number,
    78→  durationSeconds: number,
    79→  costFactors: any,
    80→  taskParams: any
    81→): { cost: number; breakdown?: any } {
    82→  // Special case: video_enhance has compound pricing (FILM + FlashVSR)
    83→  if (taskType === 'video_enhance') {
    84→    return calculateVideoEnhanceCost(taskParams);
    85→  }
    86→
    87→  let totalCost;
    88→  if (billingType === 'per_unit') {
    89→    totalCost = unitCost || 0;
    90→  } else {
    91→    totalCost = baseCostPerSecond * durationSeconds;
    92→  }
    93→
    94→  // Apply cost factors regardless of billing type
    95→  if (costFactors) {
    96→    if (costFactors.resolution && taskParams.resolution) {
    97→      const resolutionMultiplier = costFactors.resolution[taskParams.resolution] || 1;
    98→      totalCost *= resolutionMultiplier;
    99→    }
   100→    if (costFactors.frameCount && taskParams.frame_count) {
   101→      if (billingType === 'per_unit') {
   102→        totalCost += costFactors.frameCount * taskParams.frame_count;
   103→      } else {

   109→      totalCost *= modelMultiplier;
   110→    }
   111→  }
   112→
   113→  return { cost: Math.round(totalCost * 1000) / 1000 };
   114→}

   401→        billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   402→        duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   403→        base_cost_per_second: taskType.base_cost_per_second,
   404→        unit_cost: taskType.unit_cost,
   405→        cost_factors: taskType.cost_factors,
   406→        task_params: task.params,
   407→        calculated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   408→        task_type_id: taskType.id,
   409→        // Include breakdown for compound pricing (e.g., video_enhance)
   410→        ...(costBreakdown ? { cost_breakdown: costBreakdown } : {})
   411→      }
   412→    });
   413→
   414→    if (ledgerError) {
   415→      logger.error("Failed to insert into credit ledger", { 
   416→        error: ledgerError.message,
   417→        user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id,
   418→        cost
   419→      });
   420→      await logger.flush();
   421→      return jsonResponse({ error: `Failed to record cost in ledger: ${ledgerError.message}` }, 500);
   422→    }
   423→
   424→    logger.info("Cost calculated and recorded", {
   425→      cost,
   426→      billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   427→      duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   428→      user_id: (task as any).projects.user_id,
   429→      ...(costBreakdown ? { breakdown: costBreakdown } : {})
   430→    });
   431→    await logger.flush();
   432→
   433→    return jsonResponse({
   434→      success: true,
   435→      cost: cost,
   436→      billing_type: taskType.billing_type,
   437→      duration_seconds: durationSeconds,
   438→      base_cost_per_second: taskType.base_cost_per_second,
   439→      unit_cost: taskType.unit_cost,
   440→      cost_factors: taskType.cost_factors,
   441→      task_type: task.task_type,
   442→      task_id: task.id,
   443→      // Include breakdown for compound pricing (e.g., video_enhance)
   444→      ...(costBreakdown ? { cost_breakdown: costBreakdown } : {})
   445→    });
   446→
   447→  } catch (error: any) {
   448→    logger.critical("Unexpected error", { error: error?.message, stack: error?.stack?.substring(0, 500) });
   449→    await logger.flush();
   450→    return jsonResponse({ error: error?.message || 'Unknown error occurred' }, 500);
   451→  }
   452→});

## Fix #2 — Atomic cascade failure for orchestrator children
**File:** `supabase/functions/update-task-status/index.ts` around lines 229-278
**Problem:** When an orchestrator task fails, it fails child tasks one by one in a read-then-update-each loop. This is a race condition — a child could complete between the read and the update.
**Fix:**
1. Read the file, find the cascade failure logic (around lines 229-278)
2. Replace the read-then-update-each loop with a single atomic UPDATE statement:
   ```
   .update({ status: 'Failed', error_message: '...' })
   .eq('orchestrator_task_id', id)
   .not('status', 'in', '("Complete","Failed","Cancelled")')
   ```
3. This way, children that already completed or failed won't be affected (they won't match the filter).
4. Keep any logging that was there — just make the DB operation atomic.
5. IMPORTANT: Check what the current status values are in the codebase. They might be capitalized differently (e.g., 'Complete' vs 'complete'). Use the exact same casing as the current code.

## Fix #3 — Stripe webhook duplicate session handling
**File:** `supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts` around lines 155-174
**Problem:** The current flow does SELECT-then-INSERT for payment sessions. There's a race window where a duplicate webhook could insert twice.
**Fix:**
1. Read the file, find the duplicate check logic (around lines 155-174)
2. The table should have a unique constraint on `stripe_session_id` (migration 20260130220000 adds it). Verify this by searching for the migration file.
3. Instead of SELECT-then-INSERT, change the insert to use upsert with `ignoreDuplicates: true`:
   ```typescript
   const { error } = await supabase
     .from('payment_sessions')  // or whatever the table is
     .upsert({ ...data }, { onConflict: 'stripe_session_id', ignoreDuplicates: true })
   ```
   OR add `.select()` and handle the 23505 unique constraint error gracefully.
4. Keep the existing SELECT check as a fast-path optimization if you want (it avoids unnecessary processing), but make sure the INSERT itself is also safe against duplicates.
5. IMPORTANT: Read the actual code carefully. The table name, column names, and exact structure may differ from what I described. Match the existing code style.

Make both fixes. Do not skip any.

   171→      orchestratorTaskId = extractOrchestratorRef(params);
   172→      
   173→      // Check if this task IS the orchestrator (has orchestrator_details but no orchestrator reference)
   174→      if (!orchestratorTaskId && params.orchestrator_details) {
   175→        orchestratorTaskId = failedTaskId;
   176→        isOrchestratorTask = true;
   177→        logger.debug("Task is the orchestrator itself", { task_id: failedTaskId });
   178→      }
   179→    }
   180→    
   181→    if (!orchestratorTaskId) {
   182→      logger.debug("No orchestrator reference found, skipping cascade", { task_id: failedTaskId });
   183→      return;
   184→    }
   185→    
   186→    logger.info("Found orchestrator task", { 
   187→      orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   188→      is_orchestrator_task: isOrchestratorTask
   189→    });
   190→    
   191→    // Find all tasks that reference this orchestrator (including the orchestrator itself)
   192→    // Must check all paths where orchestrator reference might be stored
   193→    let query;
   194→    
   195→    if (isOrchestratorTask) {
   196→      // If the failed task IS the orchestrator, find all children that reference it
   197→      query = supabaseAdmin
   198→        .from("tasks")
   199→        .select("id, task_type, status, params")
   200→        .or(buildSubTaskFilter(orchestratorTaskId))
   201→        .neq("id", failedTaskId)
   202→        .neq("status", "Failed")
   203→        .neq("status", "Cancelled")
   204→        .neq("status", "Complete");
   205→    } else {
   206→      // If a child task failed, find orchestrator + all siblings
   207→      query = supabaseAdmin
   208→        .from("tasks")
   209→        .select("id, task_type, status, params")
   210→        .or(`id.eq.${orchestratorTaskId},${buildSubTaskFilter(orchestratorTaskId)}`)
   211→        .neq("status", "Failed")
   212→        .neq("status", "Cancelled")
   213→        .neq("status", "Complete");
   214→    }
   215→    
   216→    const { data: relatedTasks, error: fetchError } = await query;
   217→    
   218→    if (fetchError) {
   219→      logger.error("Error fetching related tasks for cascade", { error: fetchError.message });
   220→      return;
   221→    }
   222→    
   223→    if (!relatedTasks || relatedTasks.length === 0) {
   224→      logger.debug("No related tasks found for cascade");
   225→      return;
   226→    }
   227→    
   228→    // Update all related tasks to Failed/Cancelled
   229→    const tasksToUpdate = relatedTasks.filter((task: any) => task.id !== failedTaskId);
   230→    
   231→    if (tasksToUpdate.length === 0) {
   232→      logger.debug("No additional tasks to cascade to after filtering");
   233→      return;
   234→    }
   235→    
   236→    logger.info("Cascading failure to related tasks", {
   237→      task_id: failedTaskId,
   238→      related_task_count: tasksToUpdate.length,
   239→      related_task_ids: tasksToUpdate.map((t: any) => t.id.substring(0, 8))
   240→    });
   241→    
   242→    const updatePromises = tasksToUpdate.map(async (task: any) => {
   243→      const updatePayload = {
   244→        status: failureStatus,
   245→        updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   246→        error_message: `Cascaded ${failureStatus.toLowerCase()} from related task ${failedTaskId}`
   247→      };
   248→      
   249→      const { error } = await supabaseAdmin
   250→        .from("tasks")
   251→        .update(updatePayload)
   252→        .eq("id", task.id);
   253→      
   254→      if (error) {
   255→        logger.error("Failed to cascade to task", { 
   256→          cascaded_task_id: task.id, 
   257→          error: error.message 
   258→        });
   259→      }
   260→      
   261→      return { taskId: task.id, error };
   262→    });
   263→    
   264→    const results = await Promise.all(updatePromises);
   265→    const failedUpdates = results.filter(r => r.error);
   266→    
   267→    if (failedUpdates.length > 0) {

   269→        failed_count: failedUpdates.length,
   270→        total_count: tasksToUpdate.length
   271→      });
   272→    } else {
   273→      logger.info("Cascade complete", { 
   274→        cascaded_count: tasksToUpdate.length,
   275→        status: failureStatus
   276→      });
   277→    }
   278→    
   279→  } catch (error: any) {

   284→serve(async (req) => {

   373→      await logger.flush();

   384→    const validTransitions: Record<string, string[]> = {

   485→        .eq("id", task_id)

   491→    if (updateResult.error) {

   497→      logger.error("Database update error", {

   501→      });
   502→      await logger.flush();
   503→      return new Response(`Database error: ${updateResult.error.message}`, { status: 500 });

   505→
   506→    if (!updateResult.data) {

   541→    }), {

   546→  } catch (error: any) {

    10→function jsonResponse(body: any, status = 200) {
    11→  return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {

    13→    headers: {

    15→      "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",

    22→// Verify Stripe webhook signature
    23→async function verifyStripeSignature(payload: string, signature: string, secret: string): Promise<boolean> {
    24→  const elements = signature.split(',');
    25→  const timestamp = elements.find(element => element.startsWith('t='))?.split('=')[1];
    26→  const signatures = elements.filter(element => element.startsWith('v1='));
    27→  
    28→  if (!timestamp || signatures.length === 0) {
    29→    return false;
    30→  }
    31→  
    32→  const payloadForSigning = `${timestamp}.${payload}`;
    33→  const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
    34→    'raw',
    35→    new TextEncoder().encode(secret),
    36→    { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-256' },
    37→    false,
    38→    ['sign']
    39→  );
    40→  
    41→  const signature_bytes = await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, new TextEncoder().encode(payloadForSigning));
    42→  const signature_hex = Array.from(new Uint8Array(signature_bytes))
    43→    .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))
    44→    .join('');
    45→    
    46→  return signatures.some(sig => sig.split('=')[1] === signature_hex);
    47→}

1→-- ============================================================================
     2→-- STRIPE WEBHOOK IDEMPOTENCY - Prevent double-crediting from replay attacks
     3→-- ============================================================================
     4→-- Issue: Stripe webhooks can be replayed (by attackers or network retries)
     5→-- Without idempotency checks, this could credit a user multiple times
     6→--
     7→-- Fix: Add unique partial indexes on stripe_session_id and stripe_payment_intent_id
     8→-- ============================================================================
     9→
    10→BEGIN;
    11→
    12→-- Create unique index for checkout.session.completed events
    13→-- This prevents duplicate credits from the same Stripe checkout session
    14→CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_credits_ledger_stripe_session_unique
    15→  ON credits_ledger ((metadata->>'stripe_session_id'))
    16→  WHERE type = 'stripe'
    17→    AND metadata->>'stripe_session_id' IS NOT NULL;
    18→
    19→-- Create unique index for payment_intent.succeeded events (auto-topup)
    20→-- This prevents duplicate credits from the same payment intent
    21→CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_credits_ledger_stripe_payment_intent_unique
    22→  ON credits_ledger ((metadata->>'stripe_payment_intent_id'))
    23→  WHERE type = 'auto_topup'
    24→    AND metadata->>'stripe_payment_intent_id' IS NOT NULL;
    25→
    26→-- Add comments
    27→COMMENT ON INDEX idx_credits_ledger_stripe_session_unique IS
    28→  'Idempotency: Prevents duplicate credits from Stripe checkout session replays';
    29→
    30→COMMENT ON INDEX idx_credits_ledger_stripe_payment_intent_unique IS
    31→  'Idempotency: Prevents duplicate credits from Stripe payment intent replays (auto-topup)';
    32→
    33→-- Verification
    34→DO $$
    35→BEGIN
    36→  RAISE NOTICE '✅ STRIPE IDEMPOTENCY PROTECTION ADDED:';
    37→  RAISE NOTICE '   - Unique index on stripe_session_id for checkout events';
    38→  RAISE NOTICE '   - Unique index on stripe_payment_intent_id for auto-topup events';
    39→  RAISE NOTICE '   - Webhook replays will now fail with unique constraint violation';
    40→END $$;
    41→
    42→COMMIT;
    43→

You are implementing 2 atomicity fixes in Supabase edge functions. Read each file first, then make the edit.

## Fix #8 — Atomic auto-topup claim
**File:** `supabase/functions/process-auto-topup/index.ts`
**Problem:** If two auto-topup triggers fire simultaneously (e.g., two tasks completing at nearly the same time both detect low balance), both could process a payment. There's no mutual exclusion.
**Fix:**
1. Read the entire file to understand the flow
2. Before processing the payment, add an atomic claim step. Use an UPDATE that only matches if no recent topup:
   ```sql
   UPDATE users 
   SET auto_topup_last_triggered = NOW() 
   WHERE id = $id 
   AND (auto_topup_last_triggered IS NULL OR auto_topup_last_triggered < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour') 
   RETURNING id
   ```
   In Supabase JS this would be something like using an RPC call since Supabase client doesn't support INTERVAL comparisons directly. Alternatively, if there's already a timestamp column being used, do a conditional update.
3. If 0 rows returned → bail (another process already claimed it). Log this case.
4. If 1 row returned → proceed with payment.
5. IMPORTANT: Read the actual code to understand what columns/tables exist. The column might not be `auto_topup_last_triggered` — adapt to whatever exists. If no such column exists, you may need to use a different approach (e.g., checking the credits_ledger for recent topup entries, or using advisory locks via RPC).
6. Look for the simplest approach that works with the existing schema.

## Fix #9 — Atomic welcome bonus grant
**File:** `supabase/functions/grant-credits/index.ts` around lines 109-164
**Problem:** The welcome bonus check reads `given_credits` then sets it in a separate step. Race condition: two simultaneous requests could both read `false` and both grant the bonus.
**Fix:**
1. Read the file, find the welcome bonus logic (around lines 109-164)
2. Replace the read-then-write pattern with an atomic check-and-set:
   ```typescript
   const { data } = await supabase
     .from('users')
     .update({ given_credits: true })
     .eq('id', userId)
     .eq('given_credits', false)  // Only matches if not yet given
     .select('id')
     .single();
   ```
   If `data` is null (0 rows updated) → skip the ledger insert (bonus already granted).
   If `data` has a row → proceed with the ledger insert.
3. Keep the existing logging. Add a log for the "already granted, skipping" case.
4. IMPORTANT: Read the actual code to find the exact column names and table structure. Adapt the approach to match.

Make both fixes. Do not skip any.

Since the `auto_topup_last_triggered` column already exists, I should use the Supabase client's `.lt()` filter for the timestamp comparison directly. The key insight is that we can do the atomic claim in two steps with a single UPDATE:

1. If `auto_topup_last_triggered` IS NULL → claim it
2. If `auto_topup_last_triggered` < (now - 1 hour) → claim it

But Supabase's JS client doesn't support OR conditions in a single `.update()`. However, we can use `.or()` filter. Let me redo this more cleanly.

Both diffs are clean and correct. Here is a summary of what was done:

---

## Fix #8 -- Atomic auto-topup claim

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/process-auto-topup/index.ts` (lines 129-153)

**Before:** The code read `auto_topup_last_triggered` from the user row (line 93), then checked the timestamp in application code (lines 130-140). Two concurrent requests could both read the same old timestamp, both pass the check, and both charge the user's card.

**After:** Replaced the read-then-check with a single atomic UPDATE using `.or()`:

```typescript
const oneHourAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
const { data: claimRow, error: claimError } = await supabaseAdmin
  .from('users')
  .update({ auto_topup_last_triggered: new Date().toISOString() })
  .eq('id', userId)
  .or(`auto_topup_last_triggered.is.null,auto_topup_last_triggered.lt.${oneHourAgo}`)
  .select('id')
  .single();
```

The UPDATE only matches the row if `auto_topup_last_triggered` is NULL or older than 1 hour. PostgreSQL's row-level locking ensures that if two requests execute concurrently, only one will see the qualifying row and get it back via RETURNING. The loser gets 0 rows and bails with a logged message. This completely eliminates the double-charge race condition.

---

## Fix #9 -- Atomic welcome bonus grant

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/grant-credits/index.ts` (lines 111-163)

**Before:** The code read `given_credits` from the user row, checked if it was `false`, then later (after inserting the ledger entry) set it to `true`. Two simultaneous requests could both read `given_credits: false` and both grant the bonus, resulting in a double-credit.

**After:** The flow is now:
1. Check if user row exists (create if needed, same as before)
2. Atomically claim the bonus with a conditional UPDATE:

```typescript
const { data: claimedUser, error: claimError } = await adminClient
  .from('users')
  .update({ given_credits: true })
  .eq('id', userId)
  .eq('given_credits', false)  // Only matches if not yet given
  .select('id')
  .single();
```

3. If `claimedUser` is null, the bonus was already granted -- log and return 400
4. If `claimedUser` has a row, we own the grant -- proceed to insert the ledger entry

This reverses the order: the flag is set **before** inserting the ledger entry, so the atomic claim acts as a mutex. The separate "mark as given" step at the end was removed since it's now done upfront. If the ledger insert fails afterward, the user is marked as having received the bonus but didn't get the credits -- this is safer than the reverse (credits granted but not marked), and can be remediated manually. The "already granted, skipping" case is logged via `logger.info`.

Both fixes are clean and correct. Here is a summary of what was done:

---

## Fix #2 -- Atomic cascade failure for orchestrator children

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/update-task-status/index.ts`

**What changed:** The `handleCascadingTaskFailure` function (lines 191-238) was refactored from a two-step read-then-update-each pattern to a single atomic UPDATE statement.

**Before (lines 192-277):** The code did a SELECT query to fetch all related tasks that weren't in a terminal state, then looped through the results with `Promise.all`, issuing individual `UPDATE ... WHERE id = task.id` for each one. This had a race condition: a child task could complete between the SELECT and its individual UPDATE, causing a completed task to be incorrectly marked as Failed.

**After:** A single `UPDATE` statement with inline filters:
```typescript
cascadeResult = await supabaseAdmin
  .from("tasks")
  .update(cascadePayload)
  .or(buildSubTaskFilter(orchestratorTaskId))
  .neq("id", failedTaskId)
  .not("status", "in", '("Complete","Failed","Cancelled")')
  .select("id");
```

Key properties of the fix:
- The `.not("status", "in", '("Complete","Failed","Cancelled")')` filter ensures tasks that already reached a terminal state are excluded atomically at the database level -- no race window.
- Status values use the same casing as the rest of the codebase: `"Complete"`, `"Failed"`, `"Cancelled"` (title case, matching `validStatuses` on line 342).
- Both branches (orchestrator-failed and child-failed) use the same atomic pattern.
- Logging is preserved: `.select("id")` returns the updated rows, which are used for the `cascaded_count` and `cascaded_task_ids` log fields.

---

## Fix #3 -- Stripe webhook duplicate session handling

**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts`

**What changed:** The idempotency approach was clarified with improved comments, and the existing defense-in-depth pattern was made explicit.

**Key finding:** The code already had a correct two-layer defense:
1. **Fast-path SELECT check** (optimization to skip unnecessary work)
2. **Unique partial indexes** via migration `20260130220000_add_stripe_idempotency.sql` with `23505` error handling on the INSERT

The unique partial indexes are expression-based (`(metadata->>'stripe_session_id') WHERE type = 'stripe'` and `(metadata->>'stripe_payment_intent_id') WHERE type = 'auto_topup'`), which means Supabase's `.upsert()` with `onConflict` cannot be used -- `onConflict` requires a column name, not a JSON expression. The existing INSERT + 23505 catch pattern is the correct approach for expression-based unique indexes.

**Changes made:**
- Updated comments on both checkout and auto-topup paths to clearly document that the SELECT is a "fast-path optimization" and the unique partial index is the "actual atomicity guarantee," referencing the specific migration.
- Updated the 23505 error handling comments to explain that this is an expected race condition (not a true error), making the intent clearer for future maintainers.
- Both paths (checkout `stripe` type on lines 160-220, and auto-topup `auto_topup` type on lines 233-286) were updated consistently.

You are implementing a security fix for the credit system. This requires careful pre-work before making changes.

## Context
There's a database trigger `prevent_direct_credit_updates()` that blocks direct updates to `users.credits`. It has a bypass: if `current_setting('application_name')` matches a certain value, the trigger allows the update. This bypass is a security risk — any code that can SET application_name can bypass the credit protection.

## Pre-work: Audit (DO THIS FIRST)

Before changing anything, you MUST audit:

1. **Find the trigger function**: Search for `prevent_direct_credit_updates` in the migrations directory (`supabase/migrations/`). Read it to understand the current bypass logic.

2. **Find all RPCs that modify users.credits**: Search for `users` + `credits` in migration files, especially in function/RPC definitions. These RPCs need to work after we remove the bypass.

3. **Verify RPCs run as SECURITY DEFINER**: RPCs that modify credits should be defined with `SECURITY DEFINER` which means they run as the function owner (postgres/superuser). The trigger should allow `service_role` or the function owner. Check what role check the trigger uses — it might check `current_user`, `session_user`, or `current_setting('request.jwt.claims')`.

4. **Search for SET application_name**: Run `grep -r "application_name" supabase/` to find all edge functions that set application_name to bypass the trigger. These are the code paths that currently rely on the bypass.

5. **Verify the safe path**: After removing the application_name bypass, the trigger should still allow:
   - SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (they run as the DB owner, which should be allowed)
   - service_role calls (from edge functions using supabaseAdmin)
   - But NOT direct client-side updates

## The Fix

Based on your audit findings:

1. **Create a new migration file** in `supabase/migrations/`. Name it with today's date format: `20260213000000_remove_credit_trigger_bypass.sql`

2. **Modify the trigger function** to remove the `application_name` bypass. Keep the `service_role` check (or whatever role-based check exists). The trigger should:
   - ALLOW updates from service_role / SECURITY DEFINER RPCs
   - BLOCK direct client updates
   - NOT have any application_name-based bypass

3. **Remove SET application_name calls** from edge functions that were using the bypass (found in step 4). These should be using supabaseAdmin (service_role) anyway, so the trigger's service_role check will allow them through.

## IMPORTANT
- Read all relevant code BEFORE making changes
- If the audit reveals that removing the bypass would break things (e.g., some RPC doesn't run as SECURITY DEFINER), document what needs to change but DON'T make a change that would break credit operations
- The migration file goes in `supabase/migrations/`, NOT in `supabase/functions/`
- Keep the migration simple and focused

     4→-- Create a function that blocks direct credit updates from users

    21→    -- Block all other direct credit changes
    22→    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Credits cannot be modified directly. Use the credits system.';
    23→  END IF;

    26→END;

    31→CREATE TRIGGER prevent_credit_manipulation

    37→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION refresh_user_balance()

    39→LANGUAGE plpgsql 
    40→SECURITY DEFINER
    41→AS $$
    42→BEGIN
    43→  -- Set application name to identify this as a system update
    44→  PERFORM set_config('application_name', 'refresh_user_balance', true);
    45→  
    46→  UPDATE users SET credits = (
    47→    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0)

    53→  PERFORM set_config('application_name', '', true);
    54→

    26→    OLD.generation_processed_at IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.generation_processed_at
    27→  ) THEN
    28→    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Timing fields can only be modified by system functions';
    29→  END IF;
    30→  
    31→  RETURN NEW;
    32→END;
    33→$$;

    35→-- Remove SECURITY DEFINER from get_task_run_type
    36→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_task_run_type(p_task_type TEXT)
    37→RETURNS TEXT
    38→LANGUAGE plpgsql
    39→-- REMOVED SECURITY DEFINER
    40→AS $$
    41→DECLARE
    42→    run_type_result text;

    44→    SELECT run_type INTO run_type_result
    45→    FROM task_types
    46→    WHERE name = p_task_type AND is_active = true;

    52→-- Remove SECURITY DEFINER from count_eligible_tasks_service_role
    53→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION count_eligible_tasks_service_role(
    54→  p_include_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    55→  p_run_type TEXT DEFAULT NULL
    56→)
    57→RETURNS INTEGER
    58→LANGUAGE plpgsql
    59→-- REMOVED SECURITY DEFINER
    60→AS $$
    61→BEGIN
    62→  RETURN (
    63→    SELECT COUNT(*)::INTEGER
    64→    FROM tasks t
    65→    JOIN task_types tt ON t.task_type = tt.name
    66→    WHERE 
    67→      (t.status = 'Queued' OR (p_include_active AND t.status = 'In Progress'))
    68→      AND (p_run_type IS NULL OR tt.run_type = p_run_type)
    69→      AND tt.is_active = true
    70→  );
    71→END;
    72→$$;
    73→
    74→-- Remove SECURITY DEFINER from count_eligible_tasks_user
    75→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION count_eligible_tasks_user(
    76→  p_user_id UUID,
    77→  p_include_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    78→  p_run_type TEXT DEFAULT NULL
    79→)
    80→RETURNS INTEGER
    81→LANGUAGE plpgsql
    82→-- REMOVED SECURITY DEFINER
    83→AS $$
    84→BEGIN
    85→  RETURN (
    86→    SELECT COUNT(*)::INTEGER
    87→    FROM tasks t
    88→    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
    89→    JOIN task_types tt ON t.task_type = tt.name
    90→    WHERE 
    91→      p.user_id = p_user_id
    92→      AND (t.status = 'Queued' OR (p_include_active AND t.status = 'In Progress'))
    93→      AND (p_run_type IS NULL OR tt.run_type = p_run_type)
    94→      AND tt.is_active = true
    95→  );
    96→END;
    97→$$;
    98→
    99→-- Remove SECURITY DEFINER from per_user_capacity_stats_service_role
   100→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION per_user_capacity_stats_service_role()
   101→RETURNS TABLE(
   102→  user_id UUID,
   103→  credits NUMERIC,
   104→  queued_tasks BIGINT,
   105→  in_progress_tasks BIGINT,
   106→  total_pending_tasks BIGINT
   107→)
   108→LANGUAGE plpgsql
   109→-- REMOVED SECURITY DEFINER
   110→AS $$
   111→BEGIN
   112→  RETURN QUERY
   113→  SELECT 
   114→    u.id as user_id,
   115→    u.credits,
   116→    COALESCE(queued.task_count, 0) as queued_tasks,
   117→    COALESCE(in_progress.task_count, 0) as in_progress_tasks,
   118→    COALESCE(queued.task_count, 0) + COALESCE(in_progress.task_count, 0) as total_pending_tasks
   119→  FROM users u
   120→  LEFT JOIN (
   121→    SELECT 
   122→      p.user_id,
   123→      COUNT(*) as task_count
   124→    FROM tasks t
   125→    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
   126→    WHERE t.status = 'Queued'
   127→    GROUP BY p.user_id
   128→  ) queued ON u.id = queued.user_id
   129→  LEFT JOIN (
   130→    SELECT 
   131→      p.user_id,
   132→      COUNT(*) as task_count
   133→    FROM tasks t
   134→    JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
   135→    WHERE t.status = 'In Progress'
   136→    GROUP BY p.user_id
   137→  ) in_progress ON u.id = in_progress.user_id
   138→  WHERE u.credits IS NOT NULL
   139→  ORDER BY total_pending_tasks DESC, u.credits DESC;
   140→END;
   141→$$;
   142→
   143→-- Remove SECURITY DEFINER from complete_task_with_timing
   144→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION complete_task_with_timing(
   145→  p_task_id TEXT,
   146→  p_output_location TEXT
   147→)
   148→RETURNS BOOLEAN
   149→LANGUAGE plpgsql
   150→-- REMOVED SECURITY DEFINER
   151→AS $$
   152→DECLARE
   153→    task_uuid UUID;
   154→    rows_updated INTEGER;
   155→BEGIN
   156→    -- Convert string ID to UUID with error handling
   157→    BEGIN
   158→        task_uuid := p_task_id::UUID;
   159→    EXCEPTION WHEN invalid_text_representation THEN
   160→        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid task_id format: %', p_task_id;
   161→    END;
   162→
   163→    -- Complete the task with timing information
   164→    UPDATE tasks
   165→    SET
   166→        status = 'Complete'::task_status,
   167→        output_location = p_output_location,
   168→        updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
   169→        generation_processed_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
   170→    WHERE id = task_uuid;
   171→    
   172→    GET DIAGNOSTICS rows_updated = ROW_COUNT;
   173→    
   174→    RETURN rows_updated > 0;
   175→END;
   176→$$;

   193→
   194→COMMENT ON FUNCTION complete_task_with_timing IS

   196→
   197→COMMIT;

1→-- Support fractional costs in credits_ledger
     2→-- Change amount column from integer to numeric(10,3) to support fractional cents
     3→
     4→-- First, drop the view that depends on the amount column
     5→DROP VIEW IF EXISTS user_credit_balance;
     6→
     7→-- Update the users.credits column to also support fractional values
     8→ALTER TABLE users 
     9→ALTER COLUMN credits TYPE numeric(10,3);
    10→
    11→-- Now alter the credits_ledger amount column type
    12→ALTER TABLE credits_ledger 
    13→ALTER COLUMN amount TYPE numeric(10,3);
    14→
    15→-- Recreate the user_credit_balance view with updated column types
    16→CREATE VIEW user_credit_balance AS
    17→SELECT 
    18→  u.id as user_id,
    19→  u.credits as current_balance,
    20→  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cl.type IN ('stripe', 'manual') THEN cl.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) as total_purchased,
    21→  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cl.type = 'spend' THEN ABS(cl.amount) ELSE 0 END), 0) as total_spent,
    22→  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cl.type = 'refund' THEN cl.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) as total_refunded
    23→FROM users u
    24→LEFT JOIN credits_ledger cl ON u.id = cl.user_id
    25→GROUP BY u.id, u.credits;
    26→
    27→-- Update the refresh_user_balance function to handle numeric values
    28→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION refresh_user_balance() 
    29→RETURNS trigger 
    30→LANGUAGE plpgsql 
    31→SECURITY DEFINER
    32→AS $$
    33→BEGIN
    34→  -- Set application name to identify this as a system update
    35→  PERFORM set_config('application_name', 'refresh_user_balance', true);
    36→  
    37→  UPDATE users SET credits = (
    38→    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) 
    39→    FROM credits_ledger 
    40→    WHERE user_id = COALESCE(NEW.user_id, OLD.user_id)
    41→  ) WHERE id = COALESCE(NEW.user_id, OLD.user_id);
    42→  
    43→  -- Reset application name
    44→  PERFORM set_config('application_name', '', true);
    45→  
    46→  RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);
    47→END;
    48→$$;
```

1→-- Add credits system to database
     2→-- Add credits column to users table
     3→ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN credits integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
     4→
     5→-- Create credit ledger type enum
     6→CREATE TYPE credit_ledger_type AS ENUM ('stripe', 'manual', 'spend', 'refund');
     7→
     8→-- Create credits_ledger table
     9→CREATE TABLE credits_ledger (
    10→  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    11→  user_id uuid REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE NOT NULL,
    12→  task_id uuid REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    13→  amount integer NOT NULL,
    14→  type credit_ledger_type NOT NULL,
    15→  metadata jsonb,
    16→  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
    17→);
    18→
    19→-- Create indexes for better performance
    20→CREATE INDEX idx_credits_ledger_user_id ON credits_ledger(user_id);
    21→CREATE INDEX idx_credits_ledger_type ON credits_ledger(type);
    22→CREATE INDEX idx_credits_ledger_created_at ON credits_ledger(created_at);
    23→
    24→-- Create function to refresh user balance
    25→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION refresh_user_balance() 
    26→RETURNS trigger 
    27→LANGUAGE plpgsql 
    28→AS $$
    29→BEGIN
    30→  UPDATE users SET credits = (
    31→    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) 
    32→    FROM credits_ledger 
    33→    WHERE user_id = COALESCE(NEW.user_id, OLD.user_id)
    34→  ) WHERE id = COALESCE(NEW.user_id, OLD.user_id);
    35→  
    36→  RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);
    37→END;
    38→$$;
    39→
    40→-- Create triggers to update user balance
    41→CREATE TRIGGER credits_ledger_after_insert
    42→  AFTER INSERT ON credits_ledger
    43→  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refresh_user_balance();
    44→
    45→CREATE TRIGGER credits_ledger_after_update
    46→  AFTER UPDATE ON credits_ledger
    47→  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refresh_user_balance();
    48→
    49→CREATE TRIGGER credits_ledger_after_delete
    50→  AFTER DELETE ON credits_ledger
    51→  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION refresh_user_balance();
    52→
    53→-- Enable RLS on credits_ledger table
    54→ALTER TABLE credits_ledger ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
    55→
    56→-- RLS Policy: Users can only read their own credit ledger entries
    57→CREATE POLICY "Users can view their own credit ledger"
    58→  ON credits_ledger
    59→  FOR SELECT
    60→  USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
    61→
    62→-- RLS Policy: Only service role can insert credit ledger entries
    63→CREATE POLICY "Service role can insert credit ledger entries"
    64→  ON credits_ledger
    65→  FOR INSERT
    66→  WITH CHECK (auth.role() = 'service_role');
    67→
    68→-- RLS Policy: Only service role can update credit ledger entries
    69→CREATE POLICY "Service role can update credit ledger entries"
    70→  ON credits_ledger
    71→  FOR UPDATE
    72→  USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
    73→
    74→-- RLS Policy: Only service role can delete credit ledger entries
    75→CREATE POLICY "Service role can delete credit ledger entries"
    76→  ON credits_ledger
    77→  FOR DELETE
    78→  USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
    79→
    80→-- Create view for user credit balance (for easier querying)
    81→CREATE VIEW user_credit_balance AS
    82→SELECT 
    83→  u.id as user_id,
    84→  u.credits as current_balance,
    85→  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cl.type IN ('stripe', 'manual') THEN cl.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) as total_purchased,
    86→  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cl.type = 'spend' THEN ABS(cl.amount) ELSE 0 END), 0) as total_spent,
    87→  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN cl.type = 'refund' THEN cl.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) as total_refunded
    88→FROM users u
    89→LEFT JOIN credits_ledger cl ON u.id = cl.user_id
    90→GROUP BY u.id, u.credits;
    91→
    92→-- Note: RLS cannot be enabled on views, only on tables
    93→-- The view will inherit access control from the underlying tables
```

1→-- Fix timing field protection in claim functions
     2→-- This restores the application_name setting that was removed in the worker_id migration
     3→
     4→-- Updated func_claim_task with timing protection
     5→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION func_claim_task(
     6→    p_table_name text,
     7→    p_worker_id text
     8→) RETURNS TABLE (
     9→    task_id_out uuid,
    10→    params_out jsonb,
    11→    task_type_out text,
    12→    project_id_out uuid
    13→) AS $$
    14→DECLARE
    15→    v_claimed_task_id UUID;
    16→BEGIN
    17→    -- CRITICAL: Set application name to allow timing field updates
    18→    PERFORM set_config('application_name', 'claim_task', true);
    19→
    20→    -- Auto-register worker if it doesn't exist
    21→    INSERT INTO workers (id, instance_type, last_heartbeat, status, metadata)
    22→    VALUES (p_worker_id, 'external', NOW(), 'active', '{"auto_registered": true}')
    23→    ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
    24→        last_heartbeat = NOW(),
    25→        status         = 'active';
    26→
    27→    -- Find the oldest, un-claimed, and ready-to-run task
    28→    -- ONLY for users with positive credits
    29→    SELECT t.id INTO v_claimed_task_id
    30→    FROM tasks AS t
    31→    LEFT JOIN tasks AS d ON d.id = t.dependant_on
    32→    JOIN projects AS p ON t.project_id = p.id
    33→    JOIN users AS u ON p.user_id = u.id
    34→    WHERE t.status = 'Queued'
    35→      AND (t.dependant_on IS NULL OR d.status = 'Complete')
    36→      AND u.credits > 0
    37→    ORDER BY t.created_at ASC
    38→    LIMIT 1
    39→    FOR UPDATE of t SKIP LOCKED;
    40→
    41→    -- If found, update with worker_id and start time
    42→    IF v_claimed_task_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    43→        UPDATE tasks
    44→        SET
    45→            status = 'In Progress',
    46→            generation_started_at = NOW(),
    47→            worker_id = p_worker_id
    48→        WHERE id = v_claimed_task_id;
    49→
    50→        -- Return details
    51→        RETURN QUERY
    52→        SELECT t.id, t.params, t.task_type, t.project_id
    53→        FROM tasks t
    54→        WHERE t.id = v_claimed_task_id;
    55→    END IF;
    56→
    57→    -- Reset application name to avoid leaking the setting
    58→    PERFORM set_config('application_name', '', true);
    59→END;
    60→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
    61→
    62→-- Updated func_claim_user_task with timing protection
    63→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION func_claim_user_task(
    64→  p_table_name text,
    65→  p_worker_id text,
    66→  p_user_id uuid
    67→) RETURNS TABLE (
    68→  task_id_out text,
    69→  params_out jsonb,
    70→  task_type_out text,
    71→  project_id_out text
    72→) AS $$
    73→BEGIN
    74→    -- CRITICAL: Set application name to allow timing field updates
    75→    PERFORM set_config('application_name', 'claim_task', true);
    76→
    77→    -- Auto-register worker if it doesn't exist
    78→    INSERT INTO workers (id, instance_type, last_heartbeat, status, metadata)
    79→    VALUES (p_worker_id, 'external', NOW(), 'active', '{"auto_registered": true}')
    80→    ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET
    81→        last_heartbeat = NOW(),
    82→        status         = 'active';
    83→
    84→    RETURN QUERY EXECUTE format('
    85→        WITH selected_task AS (
    86→            -- Find the oldest task for a project this user owns
    87→            SELECT t.id
    88→            FROM %I t
    89→            -- Join to projects to check ownership
    90→            INNER JOIN projects p ON t.project_id = p.id
    91→            WHERE
    92→                t.status = ''Queued''
    93→                AND p.user_id = $2::uuid -- CRITICAL: Check the project''s user_id
    94→                AND (t.dependant_on IS NULL OR EXISTS (
    95→                    SELECT 1 FROM %I d WHERE d.id = t.dependant_on AND d.status = ''Complete''
    96→                ))
    97→            ORDER BY t.created_at ASC
    98→            LIMIT 1
    99→            FOR UPDATE OF t SKIP LOCKED
   100→        ),
   101→        updated_task AS (
   102→            -- Atomically update the status, set worker_id, and generation_started_at
   103→            UPDATE %I
   104→            SET status = ''In Progress'', 
   105→                updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
   106→                generation_started_at = NOW(),
   107→                worker_id = $1
   108→            WHERE id = (SELECT st.id FROM selected_task st)
   109→            RETURNING id, params, task_type, project_id
   110→        )
   111→        -- Return the claimed task
   112→        SELECT 
   113→            ut.id::text AS task_id_out,
   114→            ut.params AS params_out, 
   115→            ut.task_type AS task_type_out, 
   116→            ut.project_id::text AS project_id_out
   117→        FROM updated_task ut 
   118→        LIMIT 1',
   119→        p_table_name, p_table_name, p_table_name
   120→    )
   121→    USING p_worker_id, p_user_id;
   122→
   123→    -- Reset application name to avoid leaking the setting
   124→    PERFORM set_config('application_name', '', true);
   125→END;
   126→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

1→-- Create a database function to handle task completion with timing protection
     2→
     3→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION complete_task_with_timing(
     4→  p_task_id uuid,
     5→  p_output_location text
     6→) RETURNS boolean AS $$
     7→BEGIN
     8→  -- Set application name to identify this as a system function
     9→  PERFORM set_config('application_name', 'complete_task', true);
    10→  
    11→  -- Update the task with completion details

    13→  SET 
    14→    status = 'Complete',
    15→    output_location = p_output_location,
    16→    generation_processed_at = NOW()
    17→  WHERE id = p_task_id 
    18→    AND status = 'In Progress';
    19→  
    20→  -- Reset application name
    21→  PERFORM set_config('application_name', '', true);
    22→  
    23→  -- Return true if a row was updated
    24→  RETURN FOUND;
    25→END;
    26→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

1→-- ============================================================================
     2→-- FIX EDGE FUNCTIONS ENUM CASTING
     3→-- ============================================================================
     4→-- This migration creates helper functions that Edge Functions can use to
     5→-- safely set task status values without worrying about enum casting.
     6→-- ============================================================================
     7→
     8→-- ============================================================================
     9→-- 1. CREATE safe_update_task_status for Edge Functions
    10→-- This function handles the enum casting internally
    11→-- ============================================================================
    12→CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION safe_update_task_status(
    13→    p_task_id UUID,
    14→    p_status TEXT,
    15→    p_worker_id TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
    16→    p_generation_started_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NULL
    17→)
    18→RETURNS BOOLEAN AS $$
    19→DECLARE
    20→    rows_updated INTEGER;
    21→BEGIN
    22→    -- Update the task with proper enum casting
    23→    UPDATE tasks
    24→    SET
    25→        status = p_status::task_status,
    26→        worker_id = COALESCE(p_worker_id, worker_id),
    27→        generation_started_at = COALESCE(p_generation_started_at, generation_started_at),
    28→        updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
    29→    WHERE id = p_task_id;
    30→    
    31→    GET DIAGNOSTICS rows_updated = ROW_COUNT;
    32→    
    33→    RETURN rows_updated > 0;
    34→END;
    35→$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;
    36→
    37→-- Grant permissions
    38→GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION safe_update_task_status(UUID, TEXT, TEXT, TIMESTAMPTZ) TO authenticated;
    39→GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION safe_update_task_status(UUID, TEXT, TEXT, TIMESTAMPTZ) TO service_role;
    40→GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION safe_update_task_status(UUID, TEXT, TEXT, TIMESTAMPTZ) TO anon;
    41→
    42→-- ============================================================================

    74→    )
    75→    RETURNING id INTO inserted_id;
    76→    
    77→    RETURN inserted_id;
